positive.prompt: Run a risk-driven development iteration for this approved feature. Choose one objective, use only the methods that answer it, validate the result, and make one coherent commit.
Run this feature with one authorized commit per iteration until the requested outcome is complete; stop only for blockers or failed validation.

Run a risk-driven development iteration for an approved feature with an event-ordering risk. Select the smallest analysis, design, implementation, and verification specialists needed, then test and commit the change.
For this Rust feature, include ownership transfer, staged startup, cancellation, and cleanup design only where those lifecycle risks affect the objective.

Refactor this complex Rust test environment without losing the system boundary. Assign module and task responsibilities, design resource ownership, preserve the end-to-end oracle, and distinguish enabling seams from the parent outcome.

Continue this approved feature after several enabling iterations. Recheck whether reusable behavior still has a current canonical owner, promote it only with authority, and choose a canonical path only after the artifact is justified.

Coordinate this approved compatibility fix. One customer's model exposed the problem, but the system also has sibling versions, pattern-matched registrations, dynamic fallbacks, and offline behavior. Establish the supported population and representative coverage without claiming broad completion from one model.

negative.prompt: I have a development request but do not know whether it needs analysis, design, implementation, review, or repository workflow. Route it to one initial owner without executing the handoff.
Design the Rust ownership transfer, staged startup rollback, async cancellation, and fallible cleanup lifecycle without implementing the feature.
Build the conceptual domain model for these business concepts and associations without designing software objects.
Choose the canonical repository paths and indexes for these already-approved artifacts without changing their content.

evals.prompt: The feature direction is approved, but the event-ordering risk is unresolved. Run a risk-driven iteration. Select only the analysis, design, Rust lifecycle, implementation, and verification methods needed to resolve that risk; preserve canonical ownership, record exit evidence, validate the change, create at most one authorized commit, and continue only if the user requested continuous execution.
evals.expected_output: One bounded risk-driven development iteration that states the objective, chooses justified methods, refines or creates only budget-approved canonical artifacts, implements and verifies the approved behavior when required, records evidence and uncertainty, creates at most one scoped commit, and reports why execution continues or stops.
expectations: One risk, learning question, or delivery objective and concrete exit evidence bind each iteration
Selected methods answer the current risk instead of completing a fixed analysis or object-design sequence
Rust lifecycle design is selected only when ownership or resource semantics create material pressure
Canonical artifact ownership, lifecycle, identifiers, and traceability are preserved
Validation distinguishes completed evidence, human-owned checks, unresolved questions, and residual risk
Each iteration creates at most one authorized commit and continuous execution follows the user's request
prohibitions: Do not invent approval, product behavior, compatibility rules, or verification oracles
Do not require every use-case, analysis, object-design, or language-lifecycle artifact
Do not create a standalone artifact without applying the artifact selection budget
Do not push, publish, or continue after a failed validation or missing authority

evals.prompt: The approved parent outcome is in requirements/approved-outcome.md. The Rust code already has focused settings and runtime-handle seams, but no design establishes the complete validation boundary. Run one risk-driven design iteration before further implementation. Update the existing docs/validation-refactoring.md owner with the system boundary, representative vertical scenario, native responsibilities, Rust ownership and lifecycle, verification ownership, and completion boundary. Treat the current seams as enabling results and keep the parent outcome open until an end-to-end flow proves it. Do not modify Rust source or tests and do not create another design document.
evals.expected_output: The existing design owner explains the preserved vertical behavior, assigns native Rust responsibilities, makes task and resource ownership explicit, retains focused and end-to-end verification, and distinguishes the completed enabling seams from the open parent outcome.
expectations: The system boundary and one representative diagnostic flow precede implementation detail
Responsibilities are assigned to native modules, composition roots, tasks, and handles without forcing class-shaped collaborators
Rust ownership covers preparation, readiness, task supervision, shutdown, joining, and cleanup for the complete validation flow
Focused, integration, end-to-end, and human-owned verification have distinct owners
The current settings and runtime-handle seams remain enabling results while the parent outcome remains open
prohibitions: Do not modify Rust source, tests, or the approved outcome
Do not create a second design artifact or a mandatory UML artifact chain
Do not declare host-safe validation or the parent outcome complete
Do not replace the representative end-to-end oracle with component checks

evals.prompt: An approved inception authorized one child-process feasibility proof. Several later iterations added reusable worktree safety, write authorization, cancellation, cleanup, and review-boundary behavior, but those rules exist only in tests and historical iteration records. A new task-metadata consumer now depends on them, and the repository has no artifact placement guide. Choose the next risk-driven iteration and explain what must happen before more implementation.
evals.expected_output: A bounded requirements-readiness iteration that fixes the original authority boundary, treats executable and historical behavior as evidence rather than approval, selects the smallest current knowledge owner, and invokes artifact-layout design only if a justified standalone artifact lacks a canonical home.
expectations: The original inception revision, approved feasibility boundary, later evidence, new consumer, and unresolved authority are explicit
Tests and iteration records remain evidence and do not silently become approved requirements
The coordinator routes unclear readiness to assess-development-input and stops for an external prerequisite when evidence needs stakeholder-visible decisions
Reuse, a new consumer, and accumulated durable behavior trigger artifact-selection and promotion reassessment
Artifact-layout design is selected only after a standalone owner is justified and no usable canonical home exists
Implementation stops until material product intent and approval are resolved
prohibitions: Do not invent approval for the later enabling behaviors
Do not create a mandatory requirements, design, or iteration-document chain
Do not create a generic documentation taxonomy or standalone layout guide merely because local guidance is absent
Do not continue implementation while the canonical intent owner and authority remain unresolved

evals.prompt: An approved recovery feature says every supported adapter must keep its configured capability shape while the live runtime is unavailable. A defect report covers one customer model, and the proposed fix hardcodes that model. The repository also contains named sibling models, revision-pattern matching, a generic runtime-discovery fallback, persisted identity-only configuration, and tests only for the reported model. Choose the next risk-driven iteration and state what must be established before implementation can claim the feature is complete.
evals.expected_output: A bounded support-envelope iteration that fixes the approved claim and supported population, checks sibling and dynamic fallback paths, compares live and offline capability sources, routes missing authority or evidence correctly, and defines representative verification without generalizing from one customer model.
expectations: The approved claim and supported population distinguish one exact model, a family, a closed catalog, pattern-matched support, and dynamically extensible support
Named siblings, revisions, registrations, generic or dynamic fallbacks, and unknown paths are checked only around the selected capability
Live, startup, degraded, offline, persisted, and cached capability sources remain distinct, and identity sufficiency is explicit

Missing support authority returns to the responsible requirements or external owner, missing current behavior stops for external recovery, and cross-component source ownership routes to software architecture design
Verification covers the reported model plus justified included, boundary, fallback, unknown, and cross-mode cases
A model-specific slice may proceed within approved scope, but it does not close the broader parent outcome
prohibitions: Do not infer the supported population from one customer topology, a product constant, or an existing test
Do not guess offline capability from live or cached runtime data
Do not recover unrelated system scope or require a standalone support matrix
Do not declare the broad feature complete while material variants, authority, or evidence remain unresolved
